text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS

- Parliament passed a bill on compulsory motor insurance, submitted for revision at the request of president Ulmanis. The are still several cabinet regulations to be adopted before the law may be enforced.
- The prosecutor general, Janis Skrastins, has asked parliament for permission to bring a criminal suit against Valdis Krisbergs, a deputy of Democratic Party Saimnieks.

- Delegations of Latvia and Lithuania have agreed to re-start talks from scratch. Both delegations said they would try to set the border question apart from economic issues. Speakers of Latvia and Estonia to meet unofficially in Palanga later today.
- The IMF recognized the results of Latvia's fiscal policy to be very good. What provokes slight concern is the course of structural reforms in Latvia and the country's trade policy, the IMF said.
DIENA
- In May, pensions are likely to be increased by around 5.6 percent. The average pension in Latvia runs at 40.56 lats.
- The parliament's foreign affairs committee approved parliament secretary, Imants Daudiss, as Latvia's new ambassador to Russia.
- The Danish Foreign Minister, Hans Hekerup, says his country tries to persuade other NATO members that PFP+ participants should be admitted to NATO command headquarters.
- Swedish professor Jan Akke Delebrandts has still not been found. Police has interrogated several witnesses, including the two ladies who were seen accompanying the professor leaving a restaurant.
NEATKARIGA RITA AVIZE
- The Bank of Latvia approved its 1996 annual report, prepared by Coopers & Lybrand. The State Audit also signed the report without any objection.
- A new private radio station, Biznes.Baltiya, goes on air today. Its major shareholders are the daily Biznes & Baltija and the media corporation Baltcom.
BIZNES & BALTIYA
- Riga Commercial Bank was awarded Chase Manhattan Bank's prize of the best correspondent bank.
- Warner Baltija opens the second floor of its new supermarket in Riga. The cost of the project is $2 million.
- The Riga Port Authority is to decide today whether it should start building a quay at the Riga oil terminal. The authority's right to the project is contested by Neste and Statoil.
SM
- Latvia's largest brewery, Aldaris, announced plans to quote its shares at the world's financial markets.
DIENAS BIZNESS

- Latvian treasury bills were auctioned at record low yields on March 12. 28-day T-bills sold at an average yield of 3.94 percent on an annual basis, 91-day T-bills yielded 4.99 percent and 182-day bills yielded 5.29 percent.
- The ex-chief of the Ventspils customs office to sue the Director of the State Revenues Service Andrejs Sonchiks for his dismissal.
